name: August Erséus
current_role: Co-founder of Legora (listed as CPO on Crunchbase; current involvement unclear)
profile: Swedish co-founder of legal-AI company Legora (formerly Leya). With Sigge Labor he began experimenting with AI for legal text in 2020, revived the idea in 2023 once LLMs could handle it, and brought in Max Junestrand as CEO. Legora went through YC W24 and has been valued at ~$5.5B+, serving 2,600+ legal customers.
interesting_fact: Legora's origin was a 2020 attempt by Erséus and Labor to use Google's BERT for legal tech; pre-LLM models couldn't handle nuanced legal text (especially non-English), so they shelved it until GPT-3-era models made a prototype work 'flawlessly'.
notes: Some aggregator sources (aiwiki.ai) claim he parted ways with the company in Nov 2024; Contrary (2026) still lists him as co-founder. Verify current status before outreach. Very low public profile. Unverified: LinkedIn snippet says he previously did data science at Conmigo and R&D at KTH. He is not listed among active founders on Legora's YC page.

name: Henry Zhang
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Axiom (Axiom Exchange, DeFi/crypto trading platform; YC W25, Austin TX)
profile: Young YC founder (known online as 'Mist') who co-founded Axiom with CTO Preston Ellis; it lets users trade memecoins, perpetuals and yield across DeFi in one app. Axiom reported ~$100M in revenue within four months of launch and $10M+ MRR, after raising only a $500K YC pre-seed.
interesting_fact: Axiom hit about $100M in revenue just four months after launch, with founders who were ~22-year-old recent grads.
deep_cut_fact: Before Axiom he worked at TikTok building generative AI for ads, and graduated college in two years while building two startups full-time (one exit).

public_contacts.value: Telegram @Mist_Axiom (published on YC launch page for DMs)

notes: Common name - identity tied to Axiom via YC page. Crypto-trading business; weak fit for energy/data-center theme but strong 'fastest revenue ramp' story.

name: Rony Kubat
current_role: Co-founder (CIO & CISO per profiles; formerly CTO), Tulip Interfaces (frontline-operations/manufacturing app platform, Somerville MA)
profile: Triple-MIT graduate (BS mechanical engineering, BS and MS computer science, PhD modelling human behaviour in buildings) and NSF Graduate Research Fellow. In 2014 he co-founded MIT Media Lab spinout Tulip with Natan Linder and Pattie Maes; Tulip's no-code platform for factory apps reached unicorn valuation ($1B+).
interesting_fact: Before grad school he was a science and technology adviser to Hollywood film productions, helping writers, directors and designers with technical authenticity.
deep_cut_fact: He competed on TV's Junkyard Wars with team 'The Geeks' (3rd place, US Season 3), wrote one of the world's first theatre pieces performed by a human-and-robot ensemble, and Wired said he has a 'steady low voice that could pacify a riot'.

public_contacts.value: Guest on Tulip's Augmented Ops podcast (3 episodes)

notes: Good podcast candidate (comfortable on air; manufacturing/industrial AI). Route via Tulip press office.

name: Marcel Birkner
current_role: Founding Engineer, leads platform engineering, Dash0
profile: German site-reliability/platform engineer and Dash0 co-founder who runs its AWS and GCP infrastructure, Kubernetes and GitOps pipeline. He previously spent four years as a Staff SRE at Instana running its SaaS platform and then worked on ClickHouse Cloud. Dash0 reached a $1B valuation in its 2026 Series B.
interesting_fact: He has led Dash0's infrastructure from launch to multiple US regions and a migration of its ClickHouse cluster to AWS Graviton 5, which he wrote up publicly.
deep_cut_fact: Between Instana and Dash0 he worked as a Cloud Software Engineer on ClickHouse Cloud - the same database technology Dash0 now runs at scale.
notes: Infra/SRE focus - relevant to data-center/cloud-cost angle. Low public profile; approach via Dash0.
